title: Sell Mineral Rights in Pinedale, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Pinedale, WY
metaDescription: Own minerals near Pinedale, seat of Sublette County and next door to the Pinedale Anticline gas field? We check the unit before quoting a number.
heroLead: Pinedale is the Sublette County seat, sitting almost on top of the Pinedale Anticline, one of the biggest tight gas fields in the Rocky Mountains.
intro: The Anticline was developed using directional drilling from consolidated pads to limit surface disturbance, which means the well surface locations you can find on a map do not always line up with where the wellbore actually sits underground. For a mineral owner near Pinedale, that makes tracing your interest to the correct producing unit more involved than in an older, conventionally drilled field, and it is exactly the kind of detail we check before making an offer.

As the county seat, Pinedale is where most of the paperwork on Sublette County minerals eventually runs through — the courthouse, the local operators' field offices, and the historical lease record all sit here, which helps us move faster on files tied to town.

sections.heading: Directional wells and bottom-hole locations
paragraphs: Because Anticline wells are often drilled directionally from pads set back from the actual target, we trace bottom-hole location against your legal description rather than assuming the nearest surface pad is what is draining your tract.

sections.heading: Lance and Mesaverde production
paragraphs: Production here comes out of tight Lance and Mesaverde sands, developed on close spacing. Individual well decline is steep early and flattens over time, so we look at where in that curve your current royalty checks fall before pricing.

sections.heading: Getting a file started
paragraphs: A division order naming your unit and decimal interest is the fastest path. If you only have an old lease, send the legal description and we will trace it through the participating area records.

faqs.question: The well I see on the map doesn't look like it's near my land. Why would I still be getting a royalty check?
faqs.answer: Anticline wells are often drilled directionally, so the bottom-hole location under your tract can be different from the pad's surface location on a map.

faqs.question: My royalty checks have dropped a lot since the well was new. Is that expected?
faqs.answer: Yes, tight gas wells in this field decline sharply in the first few years before leveling off. We price against the actual current stage of that curve.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests that are inside a participating area but the specific well hasn't been drilled on my exact tract?
faqs.answer: Yes, pooled interests inside an established participating area are common, and we evaluate them based on the unit's overall production.

faqs.question: Does being the county seat make my file easier to process?
faqs.answer: It can help — records and title history for Sublette County tracts are centralized here, which usually speeds up our review.
